question: What will be the simple interest (in ₹) for 3 months on ₹1,200 at a monthly interest rate of 4%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Monthly Interest = 4% of ∞1200 = ₹48

Since interest is simple, it remains constant every month.

Total Interest for 3 months = ₹48 × 3 = ₹144

**∴ The correct answer is ₹144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,200

Rate (R) = 4% per month

Time (T) = 3 months

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Matching Rule

In the simple interest formula, the unit of Time (T) must strictly match the period of the Interest Rate (R). Here, since the rate is per month, the time must also be in months to directly use the formula without conversion.

Annual Rate Conversion

If the given rate was an annual rate, it would need to be divided by 12 to find the monthly interest. E.g., an annual rate of 12% means a monthly rate of 12 ÷ 12 = 1% per month.

Amount Calculation

The final Amount (A) represents the total accrued money after the given time period. Formula: A = P + SI. For this specific case, the Amount would be ₹1200 + ₹144 = ₹1344.
